heading: Quantum Computing Intelligence
subheading: Pure-plays, hedged giants & the road to commercial advantage
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Quantum pure-plays trade at extreme valuations (P/S ~64–497×) and are highly speculative — position sizing matters more here than anywhere else on this hub. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: A sharp Sept 1-2 selloff as Treasury yields jumped and growth stocks sold off broadly (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave, Quantum Computing Inc. all fell in premarket) mostly reversed by Sept 4: IonQ +1.28% to $39.52, Rigetti +0.13% to $15.20, D-Wave -1.43% to $16.58. Net change from the Aug 28 close is small — a calmer week than the prior two, but the pattern of macro-driven whipsaws continues

IBM shipped its Nighthawk r2 QPU — 120 qubits, 218 tunable couplers, and a dissipative qubit-reset design delivering 25× the circuit throughput of its Heron systems (100,000+ circuits/sec) — arriving ahead of IBM's own published roadmap. Same week, Quantinuum signed a non-binding MOU with Saudi Aramco, and the D-Wave securities-litigation investigation widened to at least four law firms following the CFO transition (effective Sept 2)

IonQ $39.52 ($15.7B mkt cap / $246.5M TTM revenue) / Rigetti $15.20 ($5.07B / $13.4M TTM) / D-Wave $16.58 ($6.18B / $12.4M TTM); Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM) at $146.12 (Sep 3), still well below its 52-week high of $170 as valuations stay stretched even after the pullback from summer highs

tiers.label: Hedged Giants — Quantum as an Option
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: Released Nighthawk r2 (Sep 3, deployed as ibm_phoenix) — a 120-qubit QPU with 218 tunable couplers and active dissipative qubit reset, delivering 25× the circuit throughput of the Heron generation (100,000+ circuits/sec) and landing ahead of IBM's own published 2026 roadmap milestone (accurate estimates from circuits with 7,500+ gates). At Semicon Taiwan (Sep 1), IBM argued the constraint on quantum has shifted from physics to manufacturing. Follows the completed HRL Laboratories acquisition (Aug 26) and July's independently verified quantum-advantage claim — a fast, compounding cadence of concrete steps toward Quantum Starling (2029)
rows.watch for: Adoption of Nighthawk r2 (IBM Phoenix) by the pilot cohort; integration of HRL's silicon-spin work into the roadmap; Kookaburra qLDPC rollout; independent replication of the July advantage claim

rows.angle: Third straight quiet week for Willow-specific news; the below-threshold error-correction result (3×3→5×5→7×7 grid) stands unchallenged but unadvanced since the UK NQCC cloud-access opening and CUDA-Q collaboration deepened in early-to-mid August
rows.watch for: Gate-operation demos beyond memory preservation; output from the UK NQCC access program; any response to IBM's Nighthawk r2 release

rows.angle: Quiet week for Microsoft's own quantum program directly, but its Quantinuum partnership had a genuinely active week: Quantinuum signed a non-binding MOU with Saudi Aramco (Sep 3, at LEAP in Riyadh) to explore industrial quantum use cases, and confirmed its Helios system is now compatible with NVIDIA's Grace Blackwell platform for real-time algorithmic error decoding
rows.watch for: Majorana milestone reproducibility (independent critiques of the topological-qubit claim persist); Quantinuum's Sep 9-10 Bernstein conference appearance and new commercial deals as a read-through on the partnership

rows.angle: Two fresh partner-validated demos this week: IonQ, NVIDIA and qBraid published joint research (Sep 1) showing a 54% reduction in logical error rates for quantum-chemistry simulations, using GSE/CliNR mid-circuit error mitigation with cuStabilizer on IonQ's trapped-ion hardware; separately, Quantinuum's Helios decoder hit a 67-microsecond reaction time — 32× inside its 2ms budget — using NVQLink. NVQLink remains adopted by 17 quantum hardware builders and 9 national/scientific labs
rows.watch for: Further application-native error-mitigation results; NVQLink adoption at national labs; new builder/lab additions; hybrid quantum-AI workloads

tiers.label: Pure-Plays — Highly Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: Trapped-ion leader; Q2 revenue $80.1M (+287% YoY); FY26 guidance $280-290M. SkyWater Technology acquisition (completed Jul 31) on track — integrated system testing targeted Q3-Q4 2026, with 256-qubit customer systems beginning commissioning Q1-Q2 2027. Two new demos this week: QC Ware/IonQ showed a hybrid quantum drug-discovery workflow landing within 4% of benchmark on IonQ Forte hardware (Sep 1), and IonQ/NVIDIA/qBraid published the 54% logical-error-reduction chemistry research (Sep 1)
rows.watch for: Stock $39.52 (Sep 4, +1.28%) — roughly flat on the week after round-tripping the Sept 1-2 Treasury-yield selloff; consensus target ~$67.68 (Strong Buy, 13 analysts); P/S ~64×, still the cheapest of the pure-play trio; Investor Day is Sept 8 — first time the company is expected to put a multi-year revenue number on the board

rows.angle: Superconducting full-stack; Q2 revenue $5.1M (+183% YoY); $541M cash, no debt. No fresh company-specific news this week beyond the Aug 19 COO/Systems Delivery reorganization; DARPA QBI Stage B decision remains pending months after Rigetti was passed over in the initial November 2025 Stage B cohort
rows.watch for: Stock $15.20 (Sep 4, +0.13%), essentially flat on the week; consensus target ~$28.81 (Buy); P/S ~380×; execution on the new Systems Delivery organization and eventual DARPA Stage B outcome

rows.angle: Quantum annealing + gate-model; Q2 revenue $3.08M missed the $4.03-4.08M analyst estimate; H1 bookings $35.5M (+1,120% YoY). CFO John Markovich's retirement became effective Sept 2 (Greg Golkov now acting CFO). The securities-litigation investigation opened by Kessler Topaz has since widened to at least three more firms — Pomerantz, Rosen Law, and Levi & Korsinsky — all soliciting investors over the Q2 miss and CFO exit; insider sales also spiked to $36M in Q2 versus under $2M in Q1
rows.watch for: Stock $16.58 (Sep 4, -1.43%); BMO's Outperform ($35 PT) stands, but four active law-firm investigations on top of the CFO transition and the unresolved bookings-to-revenue conversion question is a genuine pile-up of overhangs; TTM revenue still just $12.4M; P/S ~497×

rows.angle: French neutral-atom quantum computer builder chaired by Nobel laureate Alain Aspect; completed its SPAC merger with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. II and began trading on Nasdaq Aug 28 with ~$360M cash; customers include Saudi Aramco and LG Electronics
rows.watch for: Shares nearly doubled on debut day (Aug 28 close $19.11) but have since collapsed to $8.12 by Sep 5 — falling below the original $9.79 SPAC reference price for the first time since listing, on no new company-specific news — with no independent public financials yet as the first reporting quarter as a listed company approaches

private_watchlist.name: PsiQuantum
private_watchlist.note: Reportedly closed a $1.5B round (May 2026) at a ~$10.5B valuation; broke ground on its Moreton Bay Central fault-tolerant facility in Australia; expanded its DARPA agreement to $125M as one of only two firms in Stage C, the final validation stage of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. New this week: partnered with Brookhaven National Laboratory (Sep 2) to develop fault-tolerant quantum algorithms and applications using its Construct software platform, supporting the DOE's Quantum Genesis initiative targeting fault-tolerant computing by 2028.

private_watchlist.name: Quantinuum
private_watchlist.note: Honeywell-backed; upsized $1.68B IPO raise at $60/share (~$12.7B valuation). Reported its first post-IPO quarter Aug 11: revenue $8M (+279% YoY) but a GAAP net loss of $597M, largely IPO-related stock comp; FY26 revenue guidance set at $28-32M. Signed a non-binding MOU with Saudi Aramco to explore industrial quantum computing applications for the energy sector (Sep 3, at the LEAP conference in Riyadh), confirmed its Helios trapped-ion system is now compatible with NVIDIA's Grace Blackwell platform, and will present at the Bernstein 23rd Annual Pan-European Strategic Decisions Conference (Sep 9-10, London). A genuinely active week on the commercial and investor-relations front, though the FY26 revenue guidance vs. $12.7B valuation gap is unchanged.

private_watchlist.name: QuEra
private_watchlist.note: $230M+ raise backed by Google Quantum AI, SoftBank, NVentures; 96 verified logical qubits (Nature) — industry-leading; NVIDIA CUDA-Q/NVQLink integration partner. Outlined a gigaquop-class fault-tolerant roadmap targeting 2028-2029 (1,000+ logical qubits, 20,000+ physical qubits). No new company-specific headlines this week; Pasqal's continued post-debut collapse — now below its own SPAC reference price as of Sep 5 — is a sharper cautionary data point for QuEra's own eventual listing path than it was last week.

bear_case.title: Years from commercial advantage
bear_case.description: Most systems remain R&D-phase; revenue today is mostly government contracts and research access, not commercial workloads.

bear_case.title: Valuations price in perfection — and swing hard on macro, not fundamentals
bear_case.description: The pure-play trio round-tripped a full selloff-and-recovery cycle again this stretch: a Sept 1-2 slide on jumping Treasury yields mostly reversed by Sept 4. P/S multiples of ~64-497× still price in years of flawless execution, and that kind of round-trip on macro noise alone remains a feature of the trade, not a bug.

bear_case.title: Insiders aren't buying — and leadership churn plus litigation add new wrinkles
bear_case.description: Insiders at IonQ, Rigetti and D-Wave have collectively sold a net of roughly $863M in stock over the trailing three years, versus minimal insider buying. D-Wave's insider sales specifically spiked to $36M in Q2 (from under $2M in Q1) right as its CFO transition became effective (Sept 2) and a securities-litigation investigation into the company's Q2 miss and CFO exit widened from one law firm to at least four.

bear_case.title: Dilution as a business model
bear_case.description: Pure-plays fund R&D via repeated equity raises; share counts grow relentlessly. CHIPS Act awards to Rigetti, D-Wave and others are structured partly as government equity stakes — another layer of dilution on top. Quantinuum's own first post-IPO quarter posted a $597M GAAP net loss against $8M revenue, and newly listed Pasqal has now fallen below its own SPAC reference price just eight trading days after a ~100× revenue multiple debut — a reminder that new entrants are still being priced on story, not statements.

bear_case.title: Winner may not be listed
bear_case.description: IBM/Google/Microsoft or private PsiQuantum could reach fault tolerance first, stranding pure-play premiums. IBM's Nighthawk r2 release (Sep 3, ahead of its own roadmap) and PsiQuantum's new Brookhaven National Lab partnership are fresh reminders that the hedged giants and well-capitalized private players can simply out-execute rather than race the pure-plays on public markets.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: IBM
positions.note: Shipped Nighthawk r2 (Sep 3) — 120 qubits, 218 tunable couplers, dissipative qubit reset — hitting 100,000+ circuits/sec (25× Heron) and landing ahead of IBM's own 2026 roadmap milestone; also framed manufacturing, not physics, as quantum's remaining bottleneck at Semicon Taiwan (Sep 1). Nudged up on execution pace; still a rounding error on a profitable, dividend-paying business.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: Third straight quiet week for Willow-specific hardware news — the below-threshold error-correction result stands unchallenged but unadvanced. Trimmed a notch to fund IBM's active week; also your largest AI-sleeve holding, so size this sector weight with that overlap in mind.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Own quantum program quiet, but the Quantinuum partnership had a real week: a non-binding MOU with Saudi Aramco (Sep 3) and confirmed Grace Blackwell compatibility for Helios enabling real-time error decoding. Held steady; also held in the AI sleeve — avoid double-counting.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Two partner-validated demos landed this week: the IonQ/NVIDIA/qBraid paper showing a 54% cut in logical error rates (Sep 1), and Quantinuum's Helios decoder hitting a 67-microsecond reaction time — 32× inside its 2ms budget — on NVQLink. Bumped up on tangible cross-partner traction; also your largest cross-sector AI holding, so size for that concentration too.

positions.name: IonQ
positions.note: Guidance still $280-290M FY26 revenue, SkyWater integration on track for 256-qubit customer systems in Q1-Q2 2027, and two new demos this week (a QC Ware drug-discovery collab and the NVIDIA/qBraid error-reduction paper). Investor Day is Sept 8 — first time the company puts a multi-year revenue number on the board. Nudged up ahead of that catalyst; still the cheapest pure-play on P/S (~64×).

positions.name: Rigetti
positions.note: No fresh operating news this week; DARPA QBI Stage B decision remains pending months after Rigetti was passed over in the initial cohort. Held at minimum size — no new catalyst to justify more, but $541M cash and no debt keeps the balance sheet a genuine backstop.

positions.name: D-Wave
positions.note: Downgraded out of the sleeve this week: Q2 revenue of $3.08M missed the $4.03-4.08M estimate, the CFO transition became effective Sept 2, and the securities-litigation investigation has widened from one law firm to at least four — while insider sales spiked to $36M in Q2 from under $2M in Q1. The 1,120% bookings surge is still real, but too much is unresolved at once to hold it, even at minimum size.

positions.name: Quantinuum
positions.note: An active week commercially — a non-binding MOU with Saudi Aramco (Sep 3) and confirmed Grace Blackwell compatibility for Helios — but FY26 guidance of just $28-32M revenue against a $12.7B IPO valuation is still the open question keeping this in Watch, not Core.

positions.name: Pasqal
positions.note: Downgraded from Watch: shares have fallen from the $19.11 debut-day close (Aug 28) to $8.12 (Sep 5) — below the original $9.79 SPAC reference price for the first time — on no new company-specific news. A ~100× revenue multiple with zero independent public financials and a stock that's already round-tripped its entire pop is a clearer case for Avoid than Watch.
